headline: All-remote DevSecOps platform company emphasizing contribution, inclusion, and distributed work.
identity: GitLab has consistently valued remote work, inclusive culture, and the principle that everyone can contribute. Altruism language strengthened markedly from 2018 to 2022 (zscore rising from -0.90 to +1.23), then stabilized at elevated levels through 2026. However, craft language—once a moderate strength in 2022—collapsed sharply in 2023 (zscore -2.61) and has not recovered, suggesting a shift away from emphasizing work quality and culture-building in favor of mission and product messaging.
fit: You might be a good fit if you value autonomy, asynchronous work, and the ability to contribute meaningfully regardless of role or location. GitLab's language reaches hardest for people who want flexibility, transparency, and a sense of belonging in a global, distributed team—and who are energized by the idea that 'everyone can contribute.'

sections.heading: The Rise and Plateau of Inclusion Language
sections.body: GitLab's careers copy has leaned increasingly on inclusion and belonging since 2018. Inclusion scores rose from -1.19 (2015) to +0.91 (2021), then stabilized around +0.33–+1.11 through 2026. The language shifted from vague mentions of "diversity" (2018) to explicit references to "Team Member Resource Groups" (Pride, Women, Minorities in Tech) by 2021, and by 2025–2026 emphasized "creating inclusive environments" and "spaces where everyone belongs." The DEI facet shows explicit demographic language peaked in 2018–2019, then gave way to more aspirational and belonging-focused framing by 2022 onward. This suggests a maturation from surface-level diversity signaling to deeper cultural belonging rhetoric, though the actual prevalence of DEI language has remained steady rather than growing.

sections.heading: The Craft Collapse and Product Pivot
sections.body: From 2015–2022, GitLab's copy emphasized culture, values, and the quality of work life—craft language scored +0.21 to +1.34. But in 2023, craft language plummeted to -2.61 (zscore), driven by a dramatic reduction in mission_brand and employee_story chunks. The 2023 careers page shifted toward product facts and company history rather than cultural narrative. By 2025–2026, craft recovered slightly (+0.29 in 2026) but remains below pre-2023 levels. This coincides with a pivot in mission language: by 2025–2026, GitLab began foregrounding AI—"the most comprehensive AI-powered DevSecOps platform" and references to "the AI era" and "agentic era." The careers copy now emphasizes what GitLab builds and ships, not how it feels to work there.

sections.heading: AI and the Agentic Turn (2025–2026)
sections.body: AI language was entirely absent from 2014–2024. In 2025, it appeared in 2 of 16 chunks (12.5% prevalence); by 2026, it jumped to 4 of 16 chunks (25%). The 2026 mission statement reframes GitLab as "the trusted enterprise platform for software creation in the AI era" and references "the pace the agentic era demands." Notably, the AI framing is paired with a humanistic qualifier: "guided by humans" and "at machine scale, guided by humans." The company also explicitly addresses AI in hiring: "Using AI in the interview process" with "ethical guidelines" and transparency. This suggests GitLab is repositioning itself as an AI-era platform company while attempting to maintain its human-centered, inclusive identity.
